newsitem.title: USA: Calif. sets electric utility cost recovery terms.
newsitem.headline: Calif. sets electric utility cost recovery terms.

text.p: The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) on Wednesday adopted parameters to allow the state's investor-owned electric utilities to recover their stranded investments, the agency said in a statement.

Through a "competitive transition charge" (CTC) levied on customer bills during the state's four-year transition to a fully deregulated electricity market, the utilities will be able to recover the costs of investments, such as nuclear power plants, made under the current regulatory framework.
The four-year transition will begin in January
The CPUC directed Edison International's Southern California Edison Co, PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas & Electric Co and Enova Corp's San Diego Gas & Electric Co to file preliminary tariffs by June 16.
The tariffs are aimed at enabling customers to understand the cost implications of choosing between service options when retail competition starts next year.
The CPUC said it will also hold public workshops to address the tariff issue and will issue a decision later this year on the specific amount of the CTC.
The utilities have estimated their stranded costs at upward of $25 billion, but consumer groups claim that number is inflated.
